ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended (most notably by Law No. 181 of 2008 extending the criminal regime to terrorist financing), and its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 488 of 2002, as amended; Law No. 94 of 2015 on Combating Terrorism; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, and its Executive Regulations; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI implementing regulations; Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992, as amended, under which the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) has issued the crowdfunding platform licensing rules applicable to equity crowdfunding portals; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT circulars; and the FRA AML/CFT rulebook for non-bank financial institutions, including mandatory ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) identification and record-keeping obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each UBO, director and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Interior or Notary Public of the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Full bank reference letter on each shareholder and UBO, issued within the preceding 90 days
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship or correspondent bank in the shareholder's or UBO's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised Power of Attorney in favour of the Egyptian incorporation attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, senior managers, platform members and shareholders against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, Egypt's national terrorism lists and the Ministry of Interior designations; mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification; ongoing transaction monitoring and mandatory filing of suspicious transaction reports (STRs) to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU); negative news and adverse media screening; retention of all screening evidence for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop electronic company name reservation and incorporation portal, integrated with the Egyptian Commercial Register and the Injaz Egypt digital services platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Arabic is the authoritative registry language. The company name must incorporate the Arabic legal form designation for a limited liability company ('شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' / LLC), and every name component must be a permissible Arabic dictionary term with no misleading connotation. A Latin or English transliteration may be registered in parallel as a trade or commercial name, but the Arabic name is controlling for the Commercial Register. Identical or deceptively similar names to existing registered entities fail the distinctive-part test and will be rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / بنك (requires prior Central Bank of Egypt licence approval)
Insurance / تأمين (requires prior FRA licence approval)
Securities / أوراق مالية or Financial Brokerage (requires prior FRA licence approval)
Crowdfunding / تمويل جماعي (requires an in-principle FRA crowdfunding platform licence before name clearance)
Islamic / إسلامي (requires Sharia supervisory approval for financial activities)
Egypt / مصر, Arab Republic, National / قومي, Central / مركزي (may require ministerial or presidential consent)
International / دولي (requires documented cross-border business evidence)
Government / حكومي, Army / القوات المسلحة, Police / شرطة, Ministry / وزارة (categorically prohibited)
Names of foreign states, heads of state, public figures, or state flags and emblems (prohibited)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On written rejection of the proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative grievance with the GAFI Investors' Grievance Committee within 30 days of the rejection notification, attaching the name-search report, the proposed Arabic and transliterated name, and the legal arguments for acceptance; the Committee must issue a reasoned decision within 30 days of filing; an extension or re-reservation of a cleared name may be sought by re-applying before expiry while the name remains available; a further judicial appeal lies within 60 days to the Egyptian State Council (Administrative Court / Conseil d'État) under Law No. 47 of 1972 on the State Council, as amended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for an FRA-licensed equity crowdfunding portal. The FRA and EMLCU require a dedicated physical office in Egypt with on-site management, personnel, records and oversight functions; virtual, mailbox-only or shared co-working address arrangements will fail the commercial substance review required for the ISIC 6499 crowdfunding intermediary licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: unannounced physical on-site inspections by the FRA and EMLCU are expected; estimated likelihood of at least one on-site inspection within the first 12 months of licensing exceeds 70%, with annual risk-based inspection cycles thereafter.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 149 of 2023 (Egypt) and Executive Regulations issued by GAFI Decree No. 16 of 2024; residual application of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, Articles 77-104 (Limited Liability Company formation and governance); Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976; Commercial Code Law No. 17 of 1999; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Board Decree No. 11 of 2022 regulating crowdfunding activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration Directorate, One-Stop Shop Service Center, Nasr City, Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: LLC Incorporation Contract (Memorandum and Articles of Association) executed before the GAFI-affiliated Notary Public and recorded in the Egyptian Commercial Registry through issuance of the Commercial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for LLC formation under Companies Law No. 149 of 2023; however, the FRA equity-crowdfunding license requires minimum paid-up capital of EGP 1,000,000 (approx. USD 32,000), deposited in an Egyptian bank and evidenced by a bank capital certificate at the time of licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation documents of the Company, including the Incorporation Contract constituting the Articles of Association, are approved and adopted. RESOLVED, that the share capital is divided into 100 ordinary shares subscribed and fully paid by the founding shareholders as listed in Annex A. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at Suite 5, Nile Tower, Cairo Governorate, Egypt, within the jurisdiction of GAFI. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, jointly and severally authorized to execute the incorporation filings, open bank accounts, and apply for the FRA crowdfunding license. RESOLVED, that all prior actions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Form Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop — Electronic Incorporation Portal (Invest in Egypt online platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GAFI electronic portal, complete the preliminary registration questionnaire, search and reserve three candidate corporate names, and secure the legal-form clearance confirming Limited Liability Company (LLC) eligibility and name exclusivity for the equity crowdfunding portal activity.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a written objection with the GAFI Name Reservation Committee within 15 business days on trademark or prior-use grounds, or immediately resubmit an alternative name selection to avoid abandonment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank selected by the shareholders (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an Egyptian Pound (EGP) corporate bank account under the provisional LLC name with the founding shareholders' signatures; deposit the subscribed paid-up capital, including the EGP 1,000,000 licensing threshold for equity crowdfunding; and obtain the bank capital deposit certificate.
required_dossiers: Utility bill or lease for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the beneficial ownership profile, obtain a compliance explanation letter from the shareholders and resubmit to the bank's AML unit; switch to another licensed bank only with GAFI notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Incorporation Contract and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI-affiliated Notary Public Office (Company Formation Notary Desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the final LLC Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association before the authorized GAFI notary; verify all shareholder subscriptions, board appointees, registered office address, and signatory powers; pay applicable stamp duties and notarization fees; obtain notarized counterparts for each shareholder.
required_dossiers: ID or passport of all shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of discrepancy or notarial objection, execute an addendum to the Incorporation Contract signed by all shareholders and re-notarize before expiration of the 30-day name reservation validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registration Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Directorate — One-Stop Shop (physical or digital window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the complete incorporation file through the GAFI One-Stop Shop; initiate the unified clearance procedure covering commercial registration, tax, and official publication; pay the official state fees; receive the Provisional Incorporation Certificate, Commercial Registration Extract, and automatic provisional Tax Identification Number.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease with Arabic translation
Managerial consent forms and sample signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency query, perfect the file within 30 calendar days to avoid rejection; otherwise, appeal the rejection before the GAFI Complaint Committee and, failing that, commence administrative judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, E-Invoicing, and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Taxpayer Services Directorate; National Social Insurance Authority (NSSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the provisional TIN at the ETA office of the registered address; register for Value Added Tax and stamp tax where applicable; onboard the company billing system on the ETA e-invoicing and e-receipt platform; enroll the company, managers, and future employees with NSSA and the Ministry of Manpower occupational safety department.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Certificate and Commercial Register Extract
Tax card application and lease copy
Board resolution appointing tax and payroll officer
Sample e-invoice schema and authorized signature card
NSSA registration form and employment contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA data mismatch the Commercial Registry, submit a unified correction request attaching a GAFI-issued status extract; late NSSA enrollment is regularized by payment of statutory contributions and late penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: FRA Equity Crowdfunding Portal License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) — Non-Bank Financial Institutions Licensing Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the equity crowdfunding portal license application with the governance manual, AML/CFT compliance program, investor protection rules, cybersecurity framework, and audited capital position; complete the FRA interview and on-site inspection; obtain the final equity crowdfunding license before commencing any regulated activity.
required_dossiers: FRA license application form under Decree 11 of 2022
AML compliance program and designated AML officer appointment
IT and cybersecurity audit with business continuity report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the FRA deficiency memorandum within 60 days; if denied, lodge a grievance with the FRA Grievance Committee within 30 days and subsequently resort to the Administrative Court for jurisdictional review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) — Licensing Unit for Digital Non-Bank Financial Activities, in coordination with the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA) for data hosting and cybersecurity requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Equity Crowdfunding Portal Operating License issued under FRA Board of Directors Decree No. 11 of 2022 (Regulating Crowdfunding for Financing Small and Medium Enterprises)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) — Ministry of Environment, Cairo Governorate Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — Environmental Registration (exempt from full EIA Report): low-impact digital office and data-storage facility; mandatory site registration if standby diesel generators above 500 kVA are deployed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; sanitary effluent discharged to municipal network per Ministerial Decree 44 of 2000; e-waste and electronic scrapped assets handled per Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020 and Decree No. 146 of 2019; standby generator emissions comply with Air Quality Law No. 4 of 1994 (Article 19) including PM10 annual mean limit of 50 µg/m³.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) fire-safety certificate for commercial office floors covering automatic fire alarm systems, extinguishers, emergency exits, and evacuation signage; structural and occupancy clearance issued by the Cairo Governorate Building and Licensing Department confirming office-use classification; occupational health and safety clearance under Labour Law No. 12 of 2003 (Articles 214-226) covering workstation ergonomics, electrical installation safety, and first-aid arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Cairo; official portal: www.eta.gov.eg; electronic services and e-invoicing portal: https://einvoice.invoice.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an Egyptian LLC must file the unified tax registration application at the competent ETA tax office or through the ETA e-services portal. The file must include: notarised and legalised certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder; memorandum and articles of association; board resolution authorising incorporation; appointment of the Egyptian manager and fiscal representative; notarised power of attorney and specimen signatures; passport copies of directors and shareholders; Egyptian registered office lease; Egyptian bank account confirmation; and the sectoral licence issued by the Financial Regulatory Authority for an equity crowdfunding portal. Upon validation the ETA issues a single 9-digit unified Tax Identification Number (TIN), which also operates as the VAT registration number. The taxpayer then must complete electronic-invoice onboarding before taxable supplies can begin.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an Egyptian LLC is a separate juridical person taxed under Law 91 of 2005 on its worldwide income, with participation exemption and permanent-establishment rules; no pass-through eligibility, no check-the-box classification, and no territorial-streaming election is available for a resident LLC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide a check-the-box regime. Statutory election mechanisms are limited to tax depreciation method elections under Article 27 of the Executive Regulations, approval-based revaluation adjustments, and the carry-forward of tax losses for up to five years subject to legal conditions. There are no hybrid mismatch elections and no fiscal unity or group consolidation elections for LLCs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulations Decree No. 66 of 2017
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration applies when annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000 (Article 22 of Law 67 of 2016); voluntary registration is permitted below that threshold; non-resident suppliers of digital services to Egyptian consumers are registrable without threshold under the electronic commerce and e-invoicing rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates real-time electronic invoicing and clearance. Each invoice or receipt must be prepared as a digitally signed XML document under the ETA schema, transmitted through the ETA e-invoicing API, and cleared by the ETA before issuance. Cleared invoices receive a unique UUID, approval code, cryptographic QR code and digital stamp. Only cleared e-invoices may support input VAT deductions, zero-rated export claims, and VAT refunds. The e-receipt module applies to business-to-consumer retail transactions. Any new crowdfunding portal must complete API conformance testing and e-invoicing onboarding before the first taxable transaction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports and qualifying offshore services are zero-rated under Law 67 of 2016 when: the supplier holds a valid VAT registration and cleared e-invoice code; the goods are physically despatched outside Egyptian customs territory under an approved export declaration; services are effectively performed, delivered and enjoyed outside Egypt; and the exporter retains the statutory document set including customs, transport, forex and banking evidence. Input VAT attributable to the exported goods is recoverable through the periodic VAT return after ETA document matching with the customs authority and Central Bank of Egypt foreign-currency records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic Bayan entry) validated by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or international consignment note showing despatch from an Egyptian exit point
Commercial Invoice, Packing List and the executed export sales contract
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate confirming receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Certificate of Origin and any sector-specific export licence where the underlying goods or services are regulated
ETA-cleared e-invoice carrying the zero-rated export code and QR stamp
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA and the Egyptian Customs Authority cross-match export declarations, e-invoice clearance status, customs manifests, and Central Bank of Egypt foreign-exchange receipts. Unsubstantiated or fraudulent export zero-rating triggers retrospective clawback of input VAT at 14%, monthly delay additional tax at 2%, administrative fines of up to EGP 500,000 per electronic invoice violation, and criminal liability under Law 67 of 2016 including imprisonment and fines up to five times the tax evaded, as well as suspension or permanent deactivation of e-invoicing privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — concurrently the monetary authority, banking regulator, and primary FX administrator under Law No. 88 of 2003 and its implementing regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains full current account convertibility for legitimate trade and service transactions, but capital account transactions remain subject to material administrative controls and licensing. Profit remittances for registered foreign invested entities are generally permitted via banks after verification of audited financial statements, tax clearances, and CBE rules, but may face rationing during periods of FX scarcity. Non-resident capital repatriation is allowed under Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law) provided the investment is registered with GAFI and the FX purchase is supported by certified documentation. For an equity crowdfunding portal holding client escrow balances, strict segregation and avoidance of quasi-deposit liabilities are mandatory to qualify as a corporate treasury operation rather than a banking activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Decree No. 89 of 2022 and related circulars, exporters must repatriate export proceeds into Egypt within the statutory period of 5 months from the date of exportation (unless a specific exception is granted). All export receipts in foreign currency must be either sold to a licensed Egyptian bank or credited to a foreign-currency account maintained in Egypt; no mandatory surrender ratio or fixed conversion percentage is currently imposed, though the CBE may require conversion for certain categories at times of balance-of-payments stress. For portfolio-type services, the relevant 'deemed export' regime may require registration with the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) prior to receipt of foreign funds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct feasibility. Offshore digital EMI/PSP providers are not licensed to open payment settlement accounts in Egypt, and the CBE prohibits non-licensed non-bank entities from holding customer funds in Egyptian pounds or facilitating local peer-to-peer transfers. Such providers may only serve as upstream technology or card-processing vendors. To operate lawfully, the crowdfunding portal must obtain a non-bank financial license from the FRA (under Law No. 169 of 2020 on Crowdfunding) and a CBE payment system license under the electronic payment law; foreign EMIs cannot act as the primary escrow agent without a full banking license or an authorized partnership with a licensed Egyptian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is typically mandatory for corporate account opening in Egypt. At least two authorized signatories — usually the general manager and a director — must appear in person before a bank officer with original identification documents, the corporate founding deed (Aqd Ta'sis), commercial registration, tax card, and board resolution. Certain major banks now permit hybrid onboarding with an initial video KYC followed by a physical branch visit; however, for non-resident shareholders and high-risk crowdfunding platforms, the CBE requires enhanced due diligence and almost always a physical interview at the bank's main branch or overseas correspondent branch. Remote 100% digital opening is not accepted for this entity type.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business classification as an equity crowdfunding portal under banking KYC policies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unconditional copy of the FRA crowdfunding license or formal application receipt; detailed business model memo proving no deposit-taking or banking activity; transaction flow diagram showing investor funds routed to a segregated escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank; AML/CFT policy manual; board resolution appointing the AML compliance officer; audited financials or equity funding proof for the portal itself.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident natural person appearing as significant beneficial owner or signatory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy with notarization; proof of overseas address; CV or corporate history demonstrating legitimate fintech/crowdfunding expertise; source of wealth statement supported by bank reference or tax return; police clearance certificate from the residential jurisdiction where legally obtainable; Jordan-approved apostille or consular legalization for all foreign-issued documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of client funds held in escrow at commencement of banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full investor subscription records for any pre-registration trial period; bank statements showing inbound investor wires and the corresponding blockchain or ledger records; underlying KYC files of the first 25 investors; rationale for the holding period; irrevocable commitment that all escrow balances are distributed exclusively to project owners on FRA-approved triggers; third-party audit opinion on internal controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential violation of the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 under CBE Rule 65 regarding high-risk clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence forms tailored to each director and beneficial owner; a documented risk-acceptance memorandum by the bank's AML committee; proof of adequate financial intelligence unit filing history within Egypt (if applicable); sworn statement on the absence of PEP status; commitment to provide quarterly business transaction reports voluntarily in the first year.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or shareholder financing for the crowdfunding portal must be routed via licensed Egyptian banks using SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for larger amounts, with mandatory FX purpose codes (e.g., code '900' for foreign direct investment inflow, or code '501' for equity injection). The capital must be registered with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the CBE's foreign assets database within 30 days. The receiving bank will generate an FD (Foreign Direct Investment) identification number, which is required for any subsequent repatriation of profit or capital. Escrow deposits from investors are to be received only through an escrow account opened at a licensed Egyptian bank or a blockchain-based payment system approved by the FRA; separate comingling with the portal's operating funds is prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and investment disbursements are executed via SWIFT MT103 (direct wire), MT700/MT710 for Commercial Letters of Credit, and MT400 for documentary collection. For cross-border crowdfunding payouts to project owners located outside Egypt, MT103 with explicit purpose code 'trade finance services' or 'service payment' is required, accompanied by the FRA-approved disbursement instruction and tax identification of the beneficiary. Within Egypt, payments to local project owners are settled through the CBE's RTGS system (RTGS-Star) and Instant Payment Network (IPN) under CBE regulation. All outbound FX transfers above the bank's due diligence threshold (typically EGP 200,000 equivalent) require a signed customs or service-provision contract, a tax card, and clearance from the Egyptian Tax Authority for proof of prior tax registration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla spot FX contracts intermediated by licensed Egyptian banks in the interbank market.
Outright FX forwards (up to one year) with the physical delivery of the EGP against a hard currency, permitted for hedging actual current or capital account exposures documented by contract.
FX swaps (fixed-to-fixed cross-currency basis swaps) where the underlying exposure is a real trade or investment transaction with a maturity matching the asset.
Interest-rate swaps hedging the coupon exposure of the escrow or the portal's own foreign-currency liquidity, subject to confirmatory documentation under ISDA.
Exchange-traded futures on USD/EGP offered through authorized brokers, subject to CBE position limits (note that part of EGP trading activity is still restricted for offshore settlement).

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) traded by Egyptian banks with overseas counterparties are not freely permitted for onshore hedgers; an approval from the CBE's Market Operations Department is needed on a case-by-case basis, and only for genuine trade finance hedging where a deliverable forward is unavailable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months from the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by 30 April for a 31 December year-end); extensions available only with approved ETA justification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 2% of unpaid tax per month or part thereof; late payment penalty of 2% per month on due tax; persistent default triggers tax lien enforcement and possible administrative strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within 6 months from the fiscal year-end; shareholder approval of audited accounts required before filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty on the company and legal liability of directors for failure to present audited accounts; repeated violation may lead to compulsory liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Renewal of Equity Crowdfunding Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) – Structured Finance and Crowdfunding Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application submitted during the 30-day period preceding the anniversary of the license grant date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License suspension until renewal; unauthorized operation subject to FRA administrative enforcement and fines; chronic non-renewal leads to cancellation of the activity license and deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and the Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: An annual confirmation statement must be filed within 30 days of the anniversary of the company's incorporation date; any change of beneficial ownership must be reported within 15 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 per violation per Egypt's AML Law and UBO regulations; repeated failure triggers administrative strike-off and potential criminal liability for directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All limited liability companies are required to appoint a certified public accountant for annual audit, irrespective of revenue thresholds; licensing conditions under FRA for equity crowdfunding portals impose mandatory audit with dual sign-off by an accredited statutory auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) are mandatory for all LLCs; EAS materially align with IFRS; FRA-regulated crowdfunding portals may be required to use IFRS for consolidated or statutory reporting where licensed for multiple activities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each LLC must maintain an up-to-date UBO register and file an annual confirmation of the register with GAFI; all shareholding transfers not involving a change of control must be recorded in the statutory registers, but any transfer or change in beneficial ownership exceeding 10% requires formal filing within 15 days; the annual confirmation must identify any ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more, or otherwise exercising effective control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $800 - $2,500 (including registered agent, GAFI representation, and licensed address services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,500 - $6,000 depending on the number of funding transactions and escrow throughput
